title: AIT Engineer - Electronics
description:
ROLE HIGHLIGHTS:



 - Title: AIT Engineer - Electronics

 - Department: Global Manufacturing Organisation

 - Location: Greece

 - Reporting to: AIT Engineering Team Leader

 - Type of Contract: Permanent

 - Working model: On-site (occasional travel for environmental test and launch campaigns)

 - Employment is subject to applicable security screening (incl. SUPO, where required).
   


WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS:



The Electronics AIT Engineer transforms satellite electrical designs into reliable, flight-ready hardware. You are the technical authority for electrical and electronic hardware in Athens: how the satellite is wired and connected, what proves it works, and what evidence exists that every build was done correctly.

You own the integration readiness of the electrical subsystems, define the AIT processes, test means and ground support equipment the facilities need, and make sure the design, the processes and the tooling can carry production to high throughput. You also feed what you learn on the floor back into design, so that each build is more manufacturable, more testable and more reliable than the last.



WHO WE ARE


ICEYE is the world leader in sovereign intelligence from space. We deliver persistent monitoring capabilities to detect and respond to changes in any location on Earth.


ICEYE owns the world's largest and most advanced SAR (synthetic aperture radar) satellite constellation. To our customers we provide intelligence with unmatched quality, latency and revisit times, in any weather, day or night. To governments who choose to operate their own constellation we provide this proven capability as a sovereign system.

ICEYE-built constellations serve customers in defence and intelligence, environmental monitoring, insurance and emergency management. We enable fast decisions that contribute to a safer future.

Founded and headquartered in Finland, ICEYE operates globally with over 1000 employees across Europe, North America, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.




YOUR DAY-TO-DAY RESPONSIBILITIES 

 


AIT PROCESS DEFINITION AND INDUSTRIALISATION

 - Define the electrical MAITE processes for building sub-assemblies and satellites: integration flows, standard sequences, work packages and test strategy.

 - Qualify the critical electrical integration and test processes, and define the acceptance criteria and standardised procedures that go with them.

 - Specify the test means, tooling and workstations each process needs, anticipating them ahead of programme milestones, and lead the transfer from prototype to series so that processes and tooling can carry production to high throughput.




DESIGN MATURITY AND CO-ENGINEERING

 - Work with Engineering from the concept phase so that design and production constraints are aligned, applying design for manufacturing, assembly and testability (DFM, DFA, DFT) and bringing harness routing, connector access, test points and diagnostic provisions into internal design iterations before the design is frozen.

 - Support internal and supplier design and readiness reviews (e.g. PDR, CDR, PRR, IRR, TRR), ensuring designs are mature and ready for transition into production, and identify industrial risks early with the action plans that close them.




ELECTRICAL INTEGRATION AND ASSEMBLY

 - Own the integration readiness of the satellite electrical subsystems, including avionics, power, data handling and communications.

 - Lead and execute electrical integration of satellites and sub-assemblies: harness routing and connection, electrical and RF connections, connector handling, grounding and bonding.

 - Own the electrical build standard, including crimping and soldering practice, connector identification, continuity and insulation verification, cleanliness and ESD discipline.

 - Perform and oversee in-house PCB assembly and rework according to defined work packages and workmanship standards.

 - Verify electronic assemblies before integration and support the floor hands-on during build, connection and test setup.




FUNCTIONAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL TEST

 - Plan, prepare and lead functional, interface and performance test campaigns at subsystem and satellite level, and support the electrical side of environmental campaigns including EMC, thermal vacuum and vibration.

 - Develop and maintain automated and semi-automated test scripts, and monitor telemetry and telecommand during test execution.

 - Act as first responder for electrical anomalies during integration and test, performing initial diagnosis with laboratory instruments and taking findings to root cause.




ELECTRICAL GROUND SUPPORT EQUIPMENT

 - Specify, design, procure and validate Electrical Ground Support Equipment and flatsat configurations required for functional and environmental testing.

 - Define the setup, configuration and validation requirements for EGSE, and verify it before use on flight hardware.




SUPPLIER PARTS AND ELECTRONIC ASSEMBLIES

 - Act as the technical authority for electronic parts and assemblies from suppliers, covering capability assessment, special process review and First Article Inspection.

 - Define the inspections and workmanship criteria required to verify electronic assemblies, harnesses and PCBAs.




CONFIGURATION, DOCUMENTATION AND ANOMALIES

 - Maintain as-built electrical configuration and traceability, including hardware and software versions, and apply engineering changes consistently to hardware and documentation.

 - Troubleshoot and resolve integration issues, and support root cause analysis and corrective actions, coordinating with the Engineering team, the production team and any other team needed to ensure schedule and quality adherence.




FACILITIES AND PROCESS REQUIREMENTS

 - Define the electrical AIT process requirements for the facilities and work with the Global Manufacturing Infrastructure team on the layout, power, grounding and test provisions that support them.

 - Define the ESD and handling requirements that electrical integration and test activities must meet, and propose improvements where the process or the environment falls short.




STANDARDIZATION AND CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT

 - Capture lessons learned from the floor to improve procedures, test means, test efficiency and build reliability as production volumes increase, and align with the Global AIT and Engineering teams on product standards and process updates.

 - Train and mentor local engineers and technicians on electrical integration and test, fostering a culture of quality and accountability.




WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR


MUST HAVES:



 - Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Telecommunications, Aerospace Engineering or a related field.

 - 5+ years of hands-on experience in the integration, testing or production of complex electronic hardware systems (e.g. aerospace, defense, automotive, semiconductors, satellites), including work on flight or equivalently critical hardware.

 - Demonstrated experience defining and qualifying electrical integration and test processes, turning them into standardised work packages, and taking a product from first units towards series production.

 - Deep technical knowledge in electronics, with system-level understanding across full product architectures and the ability to spot issues across the interfaces between design, production and operations.

 - Demonstrated ownership of functional and electrical test campaigns, from specification through execution to reporting.

 - Practical mastery of electrical integration: harness routing and connection, crimping and soldering practice, connector identification, continuity and insulation verification.

 - Working knowledge of satellite power subsystems, including batteries, power distribution and the handling and safety constraints that come with them, sufficient to integrate and test them on flight hardware.

 - Experience specifying, designing or validating EGSE or comparable test equipment.

 - Proficiency developing and executing automated or semi-automated test scripts (Python or equivalent).

 - Hands-on troubleshooting of complex electronic systems with laboratory instruments, and the ability to read electrical schematics, interface control documents and technical specifications.

 - Strong track record of enabling design for manufacturing, assembly and testability (DFM, DFA, DFT), working alongside design teams rather than after them.

 - Familiarity with verification and configuration management in complex hardware industries, including root cause analysis and non-conformance ownership through to closure.

 - Working knowledge of cleanroom and ESD discipline. Integration in Athens is typically ISO 8, with ISO 7 and ISO 5 environments also possible.

 - Experience in multidisciplinary engineering environments, mentoring engineers or technicians, and communicating clearly with designers, production leads and executive stakeholders.

 - Strong communication skills in English (written & spoken).
   


NICE TO HAVES:


 - Familiarity with electronics workmanship standards: IPC-A-610, IPC/WHMA-A-620, J-STD-001.

 - Familiarity with EN 9100 and ECSS standards as applied to space hardware.

 - RF integration and test experience, including connector care, cable loss and measurement practice.

 - Embedded systems and hardware interfaces (SPI, UART, I2C, CAN, Ethernet), and familiarity with Linux.

 - Experience supporting environmental test campaigns from the electrical side (EMC, thermal vacuum, vibration).

 - Familiarity with PLM, ERP, Manufacturo (MES) or Jira for build records and configuration control.

 - Launch campaign experience.
   


APPLICATION PROCESS

 - Talent Acquisition Interview

 - Hiring Manager General Interview

 - Technical Interview (onsite or virtual), including a Technical Challenge

 - Leadership & Hiring Team Interview
   
   


WORKING AT ICEYE

At ICEYE, you’ll join a diverse and highly engaged team united by the ambition to make the impossible possible. As a global scale-up, we combine speed and ambition with the opportunity to take real ownership from day one. Your growth, wellbeing, and success are a priority, with continuous professional development, training opportunities, and a culture where collaboration is how we win.


HOW WE WORK (OUR VALUES)

Make the impossible possible: We set ambitious goals and stay calm under pressure. We bring grit, optimism, and ownership when things get hard, and we keep moving until we find a way.

 - Be curious: Go deep, ask questions, listen carefully, and think critically. Understand the “why” behind decisions.

 - See the big picture: Stay close to what’s happening across the company so you can make better decisions. Consider how your work affects others.

 - Drive effective teamwork: Create psychological safety, invite different perspectives, and build inclusive teams. There are no bad questions.

 - Act as one team: We win together. We match tasks to the right owner and stay agile as priorities shift.

 - Have fun:  What we do matters—and it should be enjoyable. Celebrate progress, take pride in results, and share the wins.
   


BENEFITS

Our benefits are designed to support your health and wellbeing, at work and beyond. We keep improving them based on employee feedback, and offerings vary by location. Talent Acquisition will confirm what applies for this role and location during the process.

Base salary range for this position is dependent on experience, and will be negotiated individually.




OUR COMMITMENT TO DIVERSITY, EQUITY, AND INCLUSION

We want ICEYE to be a place where people can be themselves and do great work. Different backgrounds and perspectives make us stronger, which is why we work to create an environment where people feel included, respected, and able to speak up. Whatever your background, we want you to bring your authentic self to the table.

We’re committed to fair, inclusive hiring and equal opportunity. Everyone is welcome to apply. If you need any adjustments or support during the recruitment process, tell us—we’ll do our best to help.

Apply now to start your ICEYE journey, and help us continue to make the impossible possible together. Read more about ICEYE and working with us at iceye.com http://iceye.com.

 - Employment is subject to applicable security screening
   
   


WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS

You own the end-to-end build, integration, testing and delivery of the developmental satellites, starting with early preparation and alignment with designers, procurement and operations teams, through the Qualification Model (QM) and Flight Model (FM). You plan the AIT timeline, lead the build team, and keep build documentation, configuration tracking and lessons learned flowing back to designers, so every future unit is faster and easier to build.

This position sits within the Testing Team. It is important to note that this is developmental, prototype satellite work rather than repeat-production integration: requirements are not yet frozen, designs evolve frequently, and the Lead is expected to resolve novel problems rather than execute a fixed procedure.




WHO WE ARE

ICEYE delivers space-based intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR) capabilities to governments and allied nations, including sovereign and turnkey ISR missions built on ICEYE's world-leading synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite technology, alongside access to data from the world's largest SAR satellite constellation. These capabilities let partners detect and respond to critical changes anywhere on Earth, day or night and in any weather, with ultra high-resolution imagery and high-frequency revisits.

As a trusted partner for defence, intelligence, security and maritime domain awareness, ICEYE's near real-time data creates a tactical advantage for mission-critical operations. Founded and headquartered in Finland, ICEYE operates globally with over 1000 employees across Europe, North America, the Middle East and Asia-Pacific.




YOUR DAY-TO-DAY RESPONSIBILITIES

Build, integration and delivery ownership (EC, Engineering Configuration)

 - Own end-to-end build, integration, testing and delivery of the R&D satellite system, across QM and FM units

 - Plan all AIT activities and the AIT timeline for R&D build

 - Manage the build team and actively participate in build execution

 - Own build documentation, including build records, configuration tracking (parts traceability) and high-level build procedures

 - Document lessons learned and give structured feedback to designers to improve build efficiency and testability

QM and FM build and system-level testing

 - Plan and own the QM system build and its system qualification activities

 - Own system-level integration and testing of FM satellites, verifying functional performance, capturing any required modifications, and maintaining close traceability to support knowledge transfer to the production line

 - Define system-level test blocks and flows with technical owners, and plan, schedule and coordinate execution of functional tests, SLC, Mock Ops and other required system-level test activities (FM)

 - Across both QM and FM: accountable for test execution readiness and progress, but do not define test cases, test scenarios or test acceptance criteria (owned by Test Engineering / relevant technical owners)

Scope boundaries

 - Does not own unit-level testing or qualification (owned by project leads / technical owners)

 - Does not own documentation updates resulting from future design changes (owned by designers); this role's build documentation, including Production documentation, reflects as-built execution only

 - Does not define system functional requirements or system test definitions, including test cases, scenarios or acceptance criteria (owned by systems engineers / test engineers)


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

Must haves:

 - Broad, hands-on technical depth across mechanical, electronics, RF and software domains, with deep expertise in at least one area and the ability to engage effectively and make sound decisions in the others

 - Proven track record planning and executing hardware build, integration and test (AIT) campaigns for complex electromechanical or electronic systems, ideally satellites or other high-reliability aerospace/defence hardware

 - Strong understanding of configuration management and parts traceability, and comfort owning build documentation and build records end to end

 - Experience managing a build or AIT team, including day-to-day task planning and hands-on participation in build execution

 - Ability to plan and hold a realistic AIT schedule across build, qualification (QM) and flight (FM) units, coordinating with test engineering, and systems engineering

 - Systematic, first-principles approach to build and integration problems, comfortable working across mechanical, electrical and software interfaces

 - Clear written and verbal communication, able to turn build lessons learned into structured, actionable feedback for designers

 - Maintain strong interpersonal connections and a collaborative spirit, bringing a steady presence to fast-paced or high-pressure environments.

 - Excel at building positive workplace relationships and navigating high-stress situations with composure and a collaborative mindset.

Nice to haves:

 - Experience with SIGINT, SAR or other RF/payload satellite systems

 - Prior people management experience, or clear readiness to grow into a team lead role

 - Familiarity with system-level test activities such as functional tests, SLC (System Level Checks) or Mock Ops
   
   


GROWTH PATH

This role starts hands-on. In the first phase, you'll share the responsibilities described above with the Testing Team Lead while you build context on our systems, processes and team.

As you grow into the role, you'll take it on more independently, owning AIT planning, build execution and team management end to end. Over time, the role is expected to evolve toward team leadership, potentially leading the build team directly. Even so, you'll stay hands-on with build execution and technical problem-solving rather than moving fully into management.

Both are high-care production lines requiring the same rigorous operational discipline and production mastery.

We are not looking for someone who maintains the status quo. We are looking for someone who knows exactly what world-class production looks like, can see the gap between where we are and where we need to be, and has the drive and experience to close it.

WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS:



The mission of this role is to be the single planning point for the whole MAITE organisation in Greece: AIT Engineering, Production, Stock & Logistics, Procurement, Quality, and the Cleanroom & Lab. You will build and own one integrated schedule that turns satellite demand into executable work across all of them. Unlike traditional satellite builds, LEO constellations demand industrial-scale throughput, modular design adaptability, and tight integration between production, engineering, and supply chain functions. This role requires not only a mastery of planning and scheduling principles but also the ability to create or enhance digital tools and workflows where off-the-shelf solutions fall short.

You will work with multidisciplinary teams to ensure on-time delivery, protect capacity, and enable agile scaling of satellite manufacturing for large constellations. Much of the value sits in the interfaces: sequencing a calibration campaign or a cleanroom intervention so it does not stop a build, holding a slot for a quality inspection, or flagging a long-lead component early enough for procurement to act. The ideal candidate thrives in ambiguity, contributes to system development, and proactively bridges planning and software capability gaps.




WHO WE ARE

ICEYE delivers space-based intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) capabilities to governments and allied nations. This includes sovereign and turnkey ISR missions leveraging ICEYE’s world-leading synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite technology, as well as access to data from the world’s largest SAR satellite constellation. These capabilities enable partners to detect and respond to critical changes anywhere on Earth with unprecedented speed and accuracy – day or night and in any weather, supported by ultra high-resolution imagery and high-frequency revisits.

As a trusted partner for defense, intelligence, security, and maritime domain awareness, ICEYE’s near real-time data creates a tactical advantage for mission-critical operations. Designed for dual use, the platform also serves civil protection and commercial users for natural-catastrophe intelligence, insurance, maritime monitoring (including oil-spill detection), and finance, contributing to global security and community resilience.

ICEYE operates internationally with offices in Finland, Poland, Spain, Japan, the UAE, Greece, and the US. The company has more than 900 employees, inspired by the shared vision of improving life on Earth by becoming the global source of truth in Earth Observation.



Your day-to-day responsibilities

 - Build, maintain and optimise a single integrated schedule covering AIT Engineering, Production, Stock & Logistics, Procurement, Quality and the Cleanroom & Lab, against technical constraints, material availability, labour and facility capacity.

 - Translate satellite demand into executable work for each department, and keep their plans aligned as priorities, designs and delivery dates change.

 - Run the daily and weekly planning cadence: publish status, surface risks early, propose mitigations, and drive them to a decision.

 - Produce and maintain the artefacts the organisation runs on: master schedule, critical path analysis, capacity plans, sprints and the visual management boards used in daily meetings.

 - Integrate new product introduction and engineering changes into the plan, including prototype and qualification builds, without disrupting series production.

 - Schedule planned downtime deliberately, including preventive maintenance, instrument calibration campaigns and cleanroom interventions, so that they land where they cost least.

 - Embed quality hold points, inspection windows and rework loops into the schedule rather than absorbing them as overruns, and flag long-lead and shortage risk to Procurement early enough to act.

 - Own planning data integrity in the ERP and MES, so that material and production status stay accurate enough to plan from.

 - Define, publish and track the planning indicators for every department: on-time delivery, schedule adherence and cycle time for the organisation as a whole, plus the department-level measures that explain them, such as material availability at kit release, inspection turnaround, equipment availability and calibration compliance.




WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR


MUST HAVES:

 - 5+ years of experience in production, industrial or operations planning in a technological environment (aerospace, defense, maritime, automotive, semiconductor, medical devices, etc.)

 - Proven scheduling capability across multiple departments or product lines, building and owning a master schedule fully.

 - Capacity planning across labour, equipment and facilities, with the judgement to state clearly what cannot be done as well as what can.

 - Deep understanding of manufacturing processes, supply chain logistics and systems engineering, sufficient to challenge a lead time or a routing.

 - Ability to hold competing departmental priorities in balance and reach a decision without formal authority over the teams involved.

 - Analytical thinking with a data-driven approach to forecasting, problem-solving, and decision-making.

 - Adaptability to respond quickly to production changes, delays, or evolving technical requirements.

 - Hands-on experience with ERP/MRP/MES systems and scheduling tools, including responsibility for planning master data accuracy.

 - Experience producing visual management for daily operational meetings, and with project tooling such as Jira, Smartsheet or MS Project.

 - Strong communication skills in English (written & spoken).




NICE TO HAVES:

 - Comfortable reading technical documentation: bills of materials, routings, work instructions and engineering change notices.

 - Exposure to Lean or continuous improvement, S&OP cycles, or APICS/ASCM certification is also welcome.

ICEYE is looking for an Operations Program Manager, MAITE Finland to serve as a key strategic partner to the Director of Space Missions and ensure the smooth and effective operation of the MAITE organization. This is a unique, high-trust role that combines technical depth, operational orchestration, and strategic support in one of the most complex and fast-moving satellite manufacturing environments in the world.



The MAITE organization — Manufacturing and AIT — is responsible for the assembly, integration, testing, and delivery of ICEYE's satellites. With over 100 people across six pillars (AIT Engineering, Smart Manufacturing, Production, Stock Management, Facility Management, and Project Management), the organization operates at high pace and requires constant alignment across teams, functions, and leadership. As the Operations Program Manager, MAITE Finland, you will be the force that keeps this machine running when the Director is occupied, unavailable, or needs a trusted counterpart to extend their reach.



This is not an administrative role. You will be expected to understand satellite systems at a technical level, lead meetings on behalf of the Director, drive cross-functional improvement projects, and ensure nothing falls through the cracks. You operate through delegated authority and influence — not a direct reporting line — and your impact will be felt across the entire MAITE organization.





WHO WE ARE


ICEYE is the world leader in sovereign intelligence from space. We deliver persistent monitoring capabilities to detect and respond to changes in any location on Earth.



ICEYE owns the world's largest and most advanced SAR (synthetic aperture radar) satellite constellation. To our customers we provide intelligence with unmatched quality, latency and revisit times, in any weather, day or night. To governments who choose to operate their own constellation we provide this proven capability as a sovereign system.



ICEYE-built constellations serve customers in defence and intelligence, environmental monitoring, insurance and emergency management. We enable fast decisions that contribute to a safer future.



Founded and headquartered in Finland, ICEYE operates globally with over 1000 employees across Europe, North America, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.




YOUR DAY-TO-DAY RESPONSIBILITIES

 

Director Coverage & Continuity

 - Ensure full continuity of the MAITE organization during the Director's absences, holidays, or schedule conflicts — leading the MAITE organization, attending critical meetings, and ensuring continuity of decisions and priorities.

 - Represent the Director in technical meetings (production reviews, PRRs, major issue escalations, cross-functional syncs) when they cannot attend, ensuring the right outcomes are achieved and followed up.

 - Build sufficient technical and organizational knowledge to step in on any topic the Director would normally handle — from production floor issues to senior leadership discussions.



MAITE Team Lead Meeting Coordination

 - Co-own the weekly MAITE Team Lead meeting: prepare the agenda with the Director, lead the meeting when the Director is absent, take notes, capture decisions, and track action items to closure.

 - Ensure every meeting produces clear outcomes — decisions are documented, owners are assigned, and follow-through is verified in subsequent sessions.



Project & Initiative Management

 - Own and drive cross-functional improvement projects on behalf of the Director — including (but not limited to) the MES implementation across MAITE production.

 - Identify, structure, and manage projects that require central coordination and leadership attention but currently lack a dedicated owner.

 - Report regularly to the Director on project status, risks, and decisions needed — ensuring the Director is always informed without needing to be involved in every detail.



Organizational Rhythm & Offsite Planning

 - Support the planning and execution of quarterly MAITE offsites — including agenda design, logistics, pre-work preparation, and follow-up.

 - Help maintain the organizational cadence across MAITE: ensuring key rituals (team syncs, reviews, planning sessions) are structured, documented, and productive.



MAITE Organizational Tracking & Visibility

 - Own and maintain a clear, up-to-date picture of the overall progress of MAITE as a unit — across all six pillars — including key milestones, open risks, blockers, and team health.

 - Ensure the Director always has a consolidated view of what is happening across the organization, without needing to chase individual team leads for status updates.

 - Develop and maintain simple tracking mechanisms (dashboards, status reports, or equivalent) that give leadership and the team shared visibility on priorities and progress.



Director Bandwidth Enablement

 - Proactively identify situations where the Director's attention is needed and prepare them with the right context — so that when the Director is in a meeting, decision, or conversation, they are fully prepared.

 - Absorb coordination load from the Director: follow up on open items, consolidate updates from team leads, and surface risks or blockers before they become problems.

 - This role does NOT cover personal calendar management, email handling, or administrative scheduling — the Director self-manages those.






WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

You are the engineer who ensures production can execute: you own the integration logic, the procedures, the technical escalation path, and the feedback loop back to Engineering. You work in a "2-in-a-box" model with subsystem designers, they own the design, you own how it integrates.

 - Act as the satellite-wide electronics expert, the person engineering and production both turn to when electrical behaviour during integration is unclear, unexpected, or blocking

 - Participate in Engineering projects, ensuring that lessons learned translate directly into production-ready documentation and PRR

 - Degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, or a closely related discipline

description:
ROLE HIGHLIGHTS:

 - Title:  Senior AIT Technician

 - Department: Global Manufacturing Organisation

 - Location: Athens, Greece

 - Reporting to: Production Team Leader

 - Type of Contract: Permanent

 - Working model: On-site (occasional travel for environmental test and launch campaigns)

 - Employment is subject to applicable security screening (incl. SUPO, where required).
   


WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS:

The AIT Technician builds ICEYE's satellites. You perform the physical assembly, integration and test operations that turn qualified designs into flight-ready spacecraft, working to approved procedures in a cleanroom environment and taking personal responsibility for the quality, workmanship and traceability of everything you touch.

Your focus is mechanical, thermal and harness integration: assembling structures and equipment, installing thermal hardware and multi-layer insulation, routing and connecting flight harnesses, and bringing subsystems together into a complete satellite. We are hiring at both Technician and Senior Technician level. Senior Technicians take on the more complex assemblies, lead frontline troubleshooting and coach the technicians around them.




WHO WE ARE


ICEYE is the world leader in sovereign intelligence from space. We deliver persistent monitoring capabilities to detect and respond to changes in any location on Earth.



ICEYE owns the world's largest and most advanced SAR (synthetic aperture radar) satellite constellation. To our customers we provide intelligence with unmatched quality, latency and revisit times, in any weather, day or night. To governments who choose to operate their own constellation we provide this proven capability as a sovereign system.



ICEYE-built constellations serve customers in defence and intelligence, environmental monitoring, insurance and emergency management. We enable fast decisions that contribute to a safer future.



Founded and headquartered in Finland, ICEYE operates globally with over 1000 employees across Europe, North America, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.



YOUR DAY-TO-DAY RESPONSIBILITIES 

 


PREPARATION AND READINESS

 - Prepare each operation from the approved procedure, traveller and drawings, and check that the documentation matches the hardware in front of you before starting.

 - Verify hardware before use: part and serial numbers, quantity, physical condition, cleanliness, protections, fasteners and consumables.

 - Prepare and check the tools, torque equipment, MGSE, lifting and handling equipment and integration stands the activity needs.




MECHANICAL AND THERMAL ASSEMBLY AND INTEGRATION

 - Assemble and install satellite structures, panels, brackets, equipment, payloads, mechanisms and thermal hardware to drawing and torque specification.

 - Integrate subsystems into the satellite, verifying fit, alignment and interfaces at each step.

 - Perform handling and lifting operations with MGSE, including satellite rotation, transfer between stands and installation on test adapters.




HARNESS, THERMAL HARDWARE AND MLI

 - Route, install and connect flight harnesses, including crimping, soldering, shielding, connector mating and identification.

 - Perform electrical verification of harnesses, including continuity, insulation and short-circuit checks.

 - Install thermal hardware including heaters, thermistors and thermal interface materials, and fabricate, install and repair multi-layer insulation, including bonding and taping operations.




TEST PREPARATION AND SUPPORT

 - Prepare satellite configurations for functional and environmental testing, including installation on test adapters and mechanical interfaces.

 - Set up and connect EGSE and test benches, support test execution, monitor parameters and report anomalies immediately.

 - Support environmental and launch campaigns on site and off site, including packing, transport preparation and reinstallation.




QUALITY, TRACEABILITY AND NON-CONFORMANCE

 - Record every operation in real time: as-run procedures, logbooks, photographs, and hardware and software configuration, in Manufacturo (MES) and Jira.

 - Perform compliance checks and visual inspections at each critical step, and complete the associated checklists and records.

 - Raise non-conformance reports for any deviation, contribute to first-level investigation, and support root cause analysis and corrective action.




CLEANROOM, SAFETY AND 6S

 - Work to cleanroom, contamination control, ESD, FOD and chemical safety rules, and keep the work area compliant, clean and audit-ready.

 - Maintain 6S in the production stations, and report anything that makes an area unsafe or unfit for flight hardware.




IMPROVEMENT AND TEAM

 - Review work instructions, travellers and checklists against what actually happens on the floor, and give clear feedback so they can be corrected.

 - Support on-the-job training of junior colleagues and share good practice. Senior Technicians coach the team and lead frontline troubleshooting.




WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR


MUST HAVES:

 - Vocational or technical qualification in mechanical, electrical, electronics, mechatronics or a related field, or equivalent hands-on training.

 - Hands-on experience in the assembly, integration or test of complex electromechanical hardware. We are hiring at two levels: around 2+ years for Technician, and around 5+ years with demonstrated autonomy for Senior Technician.

 - Practical skill in precision mechanical assembly and thermal hardware installation, working to drawings and torque specifications.

 - Practical skill in harness work: crimping, soldering, shielding, connector mating and routing.

 - Ability to read and work from mechanical and electrical drawings, wiring diagrams, procedures and work instructions.

 - Experience with electrical verification, including continuity, insulation and short-circuit checks.

 - Understanding of cleanroom, contamination control and ESD requirements.

 - Discipline in documentation and traceability, recording work performed in real time rather than afterwards.

 - Experience raising and documenting non-conformances.

 - Comfortable using an MES and Jira for work records. We use Manufacturo and Jira; experience with equivalent systems is fine.

 - Hands-on mindset with strong attention to detail, and the judgement to stop and ask rather than proceed on an assumption.

 - Strong communication skills in English (written & spoken).




NICE TO HAVES:

 - Experience on flight hardware in a satellite or other space environment.

 - Multi-layer insulation fabrication and installation experience.

 - Familiarity with workmanship standards such as IPC-A-610, IPC J-STD-001, IPC-7711/7721 or IPC/WHMA-A-620.

 - Familiarity with ECSS, NASA or military quality standards.

 - Experience supporting functional test: EGSE connection, test sequence execution and telemetry monitoring.

 - Experience with environmental test campaigns (vibration, thermal vacuum) or launch campaigns.

 - Awareness of 6S and good practice in production area organisation.




APPLICATION PROCESS

 - Talent Acquisition Interview

 - Hiring Manager General Interview

 - Technical Interview (onsite or virtual), including a Technical Challenge

 - Leadership & Hiring Team Interview




WORKING AT ICEYE

The Mission of the AOCS Systems Engineer

 

You ensure that our satellites always point towards the right direction enabling high-quality images.

This role is within AOCS Domain where we are responsible for maintaining attitude and orbit. Your job will be to work closely with production teams, operation teams and software teams to ensure smooth and performant operation of our ADCS and propulsion systems in orbit and on ground. Expect to be involved in the complete lifecycle of the system - from design phases of future ICEYE satellite generations to maintenance of existing systems we, and our customers operate.

You will have a chance to have a direct impact on our mission success as performance and reliability of the AOCS system directly affects the amount and quality of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data we deliver to our customers.

 
 


WHO WE ARE


ICEYE is the world leader in sovereign intelligence from space. We deliver persistent monitoring capabilities to detect and respond to changes in any location on Earth.

 

ICEYE owns the world's largest and most advanced SAR (synthetic aperture radar) satellite constellation. To our customers we provide intelligence with unmatched quality, latency and revisit times, in any weather, day or night. To governments who choose to operate their own constellation we provide this proven capability as a sovereign system.

 

ICEYE-built constellations serve customers in defence and intelligence, environmental monitoring, insurance and emergency management. We enable fast decisions that contribute to a safer future.

 

Founded and headquartered in Finland, ICEYE operates globally with over 1000 employees across Europe, North America, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.



YOUR DAY-TO-DAY RESPONSIBILITIES

 

 - Expected Outcomes:
   
   1. Increased Imaging Performance and Mission Success. You will help driving the performance of our AOCS systems by:
      - Driving selection of future AOCS hardware components.
      - Characterizing and validating existing AOCS performance by designing and executing in-orbit experiments and analyzing telemetry data with the help of analysis software you develop.
      - Developing software tools to predict performance of our future AOCS systems.
   
   2. Maximized AOCS Availability. You will ensure that our systems perform as expected within their design envelope by:
      - Maintaining verification procedures and working closely with production and testing teams in implementing process improvements and new test jigs.
      - Debugging on-orbit anomalies requiring deep system system understanding and systematic approach towards pinning the root-cause. Understanding an anomaly is a first step towards preventing it in the future.
      - Supporting software teams in implementing changes to software to prevent repetition of known issues.
      - Work on software tools helping debug AOCS anomalies as they happen.
    
   
   3. Robust and Predictable AOCS Operations. You will help the team establish and evolve internal processes for anomaly handling and resolution.

 - Strong understanding of underlying principles of operation and failure modes of sensors and actuators used in AOCS: reaction wheels, magnetorquers, star trackers, gyroscopes, magnetometers, GNSS.

 - Strong understanding of performance drivers of AOCS systems.

 - Proven track record of owning cross-domain systems involving feedback control loops over their complete lifecycle including maintenance and operations.

 - Demonstrated broad knowledge across multiple engineering disciplines including controls, mechanical and electronics. AOCS is an electromechanical system in the and requires broad perspective to understand it fully

This is an early-stage, high-autonomy role where you will help define the architecture and direction of a platform that sits at the intersection of software engineering, applied mathematics, and real-world intelligence operations.




WHO WE ARE

ICEYE delivers space-based intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) capabilities to governments and allied nations. YOUR DAY-TO-DAY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Tasking and Planning Engines. Orbit propagation, pass prediction, acquisition geometry, sensor configuration parameters, and coverage footprint computation. Applied science mathematics turned into operational capability via Software.

 - Platform Services. Backend services handling task management. Event-driven workers performing opportunity calculation and synchronising state asynchronously via NATS JetStream. PostgreSQL for persistence. Responsiveness and resilience at the service of the mission.

 - Engineering Interfaces. Robust and evolvable APIs and UIs that enable engineers to visualise passes, compare collection plans, plan tasks, and self-service their access to space.

 - Whatever the future brings. Multi-sensor coordination, processing pipeline integration, new collection strategies, and capabilities that will emerge from close collaboration with users. You will help define the direction, not just execute it.




WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

Must haves:

 - Strong software engineering fundamentals. You design decoupled, maintainable, resilient, performant systems. You can reason about concurrency and how transactions work. You know about CAP and regularly make deliberate trade-offs between Consistency and Availability. You understand the difference between “At most once”, “At least once” and how to design systems around those guarantees.

 - Fluency with AI-assisted engineering. You treat AI as a standard part of your toolkit, not a novelty or a threat. You use it across the whole of your work (design exploration, code, tests, documentation, debugging, reviewing unfamiliar codebases) and you have a feel for where it accelerates you and where it quietly costs you time. Crucially, you stay accountable for the output: you know how to prompt and scope a task well, how to verify what comes back, and how to keep the guarantees that production demands. You are curious about improving the way you and your team work with these tools, and you help others get better at it.

 - Production experience. You have designed, built, and operated services in production: REST APIs, relational databases, and asynchronous workers. You know how to make your systems observable and resilient. You understand what production demands beyond making things work locally.

 - Fast learner in technical domains. This role involves orbital mechanics, RF physics, and geospatial data. You don’t need to come in knowing these — but you do need to be the kind of engineer who can pick up a new domain quickly, ask sharp questions, and start contributing before you’ve mastered every detail.

 - Ability to work from ambiguity. You can take a loosely defined operational need (e.g. “we need users to de-conflict between competing collection plans”) and turn it into concrete engineering work. You ask the right questions, make well-reasoned decisions, and adjust when new information arrives.

 - Effective communication across domains. You will work alongside people who think in many different ways and work in different contexts. You can listen carefully, ask precise questions, and articulate technical tradeoffs in terms that everybody can understand, and adjust to your audience accordingly.

Nice to haves:

 - Event-driven architecture. Experience with NATS, Kafka, SQS, or similar. Understanding of at-least-once delivery, idempotency, and the practical tradeoffs of asynchronous service communication.

As a trusted partner for defense, intelligence, security, and maritime domain awareness, ICEYE’s near real-time data creates a tactical advantage for mission-critical operations. Designed for dual use, the platform also serves civil protection and commercial users for natural-catastrophe intelligence, insurance, maritime monitoring (including oil-spill detection), and finance, contributing to global security and community resilience.

This is the kind of project designers wait years for. You'll be the design lead and hands-on builder on one of the most exciting products we're working on: a largely greenfield space where AI and LLMs meet serious data intelligence and where the problems are genuinely hard, the kind nobody has solved before, because the product itself is new territory. We can't say much more here (some things we build, we keep quiet about) but if the idea of turning cutting-edge intelligence into something people can actually use makes your fingers itch, this is it. You won't inherit a design system or a roadmap but you'll shape both. And you won't do it alone: we're building a world-class design team from a small core and early hires like you set the bar for everyone who comes after. This role is for a builder, an IC who gets their energy from making things, not managing them



WHO WE ARE

ICEYE delivers space-based intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) capabilities to governments and allied nations. This includes sovereign and turnkey ISR missions leveraging ICEYE’s world-leading synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite technology, as well as access to data from the world’s largest SAR satellite constellation. These capabilities enable partners to detect and respond to critical changes anywhere on Earth with unprecedented speed and accuracy, day or night and in any weather, supported by ultra high-resolution imagery and high-frequency revisits.

YOUR DAY-TO-DAY RESPONSIBILITIES:

 - Own design end to end for the product: from fuzzy problem to research to concept to polished, shipped UI. No handoffs, no "that's another team's job."

 - Get out of the building (or into the ground station). Talk to users regularly, watch how they work and turn what you learn into design decisions everyone can get behind.

 - Make the complex feel simple. Take AI, LLM and data-heavy workflows and turn them into experiences that feel obvious in hindsight.

 - Prototype fast and often. Test ideas with real users and real data before we commit engineering time and kill your darlings when the evidence says so.

 - Work elbow to elbow with engineers, data scientists and product. You're in the room when problems get framed, not just when screens get requested.

 - Set the design foundations. As one of the first designers on this product, you'll shape the patterns, quality bar and ways of working that everyone after you builds on.

 - Push the craft. Sweat the details, raise the bar on every release and give (and take) sharp design feedback.




WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

description:

WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS:

We don't have a design system. What we have is a set of products built fast, for users who needed the imagery yesterday, that share a brand without sharing much else. Buttons that quietly disagree with each other. Spacing as a matter of personal taste. Several defensible ways to build a table, none of them the same. Nobody was sloppy - this is what shipping under real pressure leaves behind, and the interest on it now comes out of every sprint.

As a Staff / Lead Product Designer, you'll build the thing from nothing. That starts small and slightly unglamorous: a Figma library people actually reach for and a design playbook that settles the arguments worth settling. Then tokens with a structure that holds. Then components in code, documented well enough that nobody has to ask you how they work. By the time it's a design system in the full sense, the hardest part - people using it by default - is already solved, because you'll have built it in the open with the teams who had to adopt it.

This is a hands-on, opinionated, sleeves-rolled-up role. You'll be the highest craft bar in the domain and the person who raises everyone else's. You'll spend as much time with frontend engineers as with designers, quite possibly in their repo. 

Real ownership. Very little existing process to inherit. If that sounds like a warning, it isn't. It's the job.




WHO WE ARE

ICEYE is the world leader in sovereign intelligence from space. We deliver persistent monitoring capabilities to detect and respond to changes in any location on Earth.

ICEYE owns the world's largest and most advanced SAR (synthetic aperture radar) satellite constellation. Founded and headquartered in Finland, ICEYE operates globally with over 1000 employees across Europe, North America, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific..



YOUR DAY-TO-DAY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Start with a library and a playbook. Grow it into a system. Early on that means a Figma library, shared foundations and written guidance that gives teams a default instead of a decision. Later it means token architecture, components in code and documentation that scales past you. You'll decide the sequence, what's a token and what's a local decision, and where the line sits between flexibility and consistency. Those calls are yours to make, not to wait for.

 - Co-design with frontend, in the code. Our engineers will build most of the components. You'll be in the conversation about props, state and composition, reading PRs and prototyping in a branch when that's the fastest way to prove a point. Figma is where you think, not where the system ends up living.

 - Sell it. Repeatedly. A design system nobody adopts is a very tidy failure. You'll make the case to product managers, engineers and leadership, run office hours, and do migration work yourself when that's what unblocks a team.

 - Set and hold the craft bar. Across the whole domain, at the pixel level, in public. Kind about people, uncompromising about the work.

 - Put AI to actual work. Component documentation, variant generation, token maintenance, migration codemods, spec drafting. The tedious 60% of systems work is exactly what these tools are good at, and we want someone with strong instincts about which 60%.

 - Stay accountable for what ships. Adoption, consistency, shipped UI quality, how quickly teams can build - not the size of your Figma library.

 - Work across a big, networked organisation. Designers in other domains, brand and marketing design, sales engineers, customers. Consistency is a negotiation, not a mandate you email out.
   



WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

Must haves:

 - You've done 0-to-1 before, somewhere messy. You've taken a design system from nothing to adopted, in an organisation that had neither and wasn't yet convinced it needed one. You know how the first six months actually go, which corners are safe to cut, and how to structure tokens so they survive the next product rather than getting quietly forked.

 - You're fluent enough in code to be useful. Reading React and CSS, understanding component APIs, running the repo locally, opening a PR without ceremony. You don't need to be an engineer, but you do need to hold your end of a technical conversation and design things that are buildable as drawn.

 - You can influence without authority. You'll spend real energy convincing people who have their own roadmaps and their own deadlines. Being right won't be enough and you know that already.

 - Your craft is exceptional. Deep command of layout systems, typography, colour and visual hierarchy, applied in dense, complex professional interfaces. Detail-obsessed in the good way: the way that makes a whole product feel considered.

 - You have a real point of view on AI in design work. Not a vibe, a practice. You've used these tools to accelerate documentation, generate and audit variants, maintain tokens, or migrate code, and you can tell us where they helped and where they made a confident mess.

 - You've owned UX end-to-end for complex professional products. Discovery through shipped product through what you learned afterwards, with a portfolio that shows the systems thinking as well as the surfaces. Expert in Figma.



NICE TO HAVES:

 - Accessibility as a default rather than an audit.

 - Experience with theming, dark mode, or multi-brand systems.

 - Data-dense, map-heavy or real-time interfaces.

 - Public writing or open-source contribution on design systems.

 - Time spent in high-stakes or regulated environments where getting it wrong is expensive.

The disposition, which matters more than any of the above: outcome-driven thinking over perfect artifacts (design is what ships); curiosity about users, about design and technology trends and history, and about better ways of working; pragmatic product judgment, knowing when "good and shipped" beats "perfect but late"; clear communication and respectful collaboration.

 - Manage technical risks, anomalies, and non-conformances through root cause analysis and corrective action, identifying and driving resolution of the issues most critical to the production line

 - Strong leadership experience, with the ability to manage and guide a multidisciplinary team of engineers and technicians, fostering collaboration and growth

 - Comfort with software in test: flight software loading/validation, test automation, and scripting

 - Strong background in root cause analysis, anomaly management, and non-conformance resolution

ROLE HIGHLIGHTS:

 - Department: Global Supply Chain

 - Reports to: Global Director Supply Chain

 - Location: Espoo, Finland

 - Type of Contract: Permanent

 - Working model: On-site

 - Employment is subject to applicable security screening (incl. SUPO, where required)




WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS:

We are seeking an exceptionally technical Manager to lead, develop, and scale a high-performing team responsible for mechanical hardware sourcing, production enablement, and manufacturing support across our satellite engineering and production programs.

This role operates at the intersection of engineering, manufacturing operations, and supplier technology, requiring deep expertise in build-to-print precision machining, electromechanical release mechanisms, COTS mechanical hardware, and the tooling and consumables ecosystem that keeps production running.

The position will define the strategy, structure, and technical backbone of the Mechanical Systems & Manufacturing Enablement category, while embedding directly into engineering and production programs. Your team will ensure reliable, qualified, and cost-effective supply for both flight hardware components and production-enabling assets, while building scalable foundations to support the transition from low-rate prototype builds toward Continuous Production Configurations.

This role is ideal for someone who thrives in a regulated, technically demanding environment and maintains strong credibility with mechanical engineering, manufacturing, quality, and supplier partners.






WHO WE ARE:

ICEYE delivers space-based intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) capabilities to governments and allied nations. This includes sovereign and turnkey ISR missions leveraging ICEYE’s world-leading synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite technology, as well as access to data from the world’s largest SAR satellite constellation. These capabilities enable partners to detect and respond to critical changes anywhere on Earth with unprecedented speed and accuracy – day or night and in any weather, supported by ultra high-resolution imagery and high-frequency revisits.



As a trusted partner for defense, intelligence, security, and maritime domain awareness, ICEYE’s near real-time data creates a tactical advantage for mission-critical operations. Designed for dual use, the platform also serves civil protection and commercial users for natural-catastrophe intelligence, insurance, maritime monitoring (including oil-spill detection), and finance, contributing to global security and community resilience.



ICEYE operates internationally with offices in Finland, Poland, Spain, Japan, the UAE, Greece, and the US. The company has more than 900 employees, inspired by the shared vision of improving life on Earth by becoming the global source of truth in Earth Observation.




REQUIREMENTS


EXPECTED OUTCOMES & COMPETENCIES;

1. Supply continuity – Reliable, risk-managed sourcing for mechanical components, mechanisms, tooling, and consumables across R&D and scaling production.

2. Technical credibility – Read drawings, GD&T, and mechanism specs well enough to shape design and catch supply risk early.

3. Team leadership – Build and lead a team of 5+, with proven management experience and ability to scale as production grows.

4. Regulated supplier network – International, defense-capable supplier base meeting security, export, and qualification requirements.




YOUR DAY-TO-DAY RESPONSIBILITIES;

Day to day, this role means sourcing and managing suppliers for build-to-print CNC parts, release mechanisms, COTS hardware, tooling, and consumables, while sitting embedded in engineering programs to catch design and supply risks early.

It also means running the team, coaching specialists, reviewing quotes and vendor selections, and keeping ERP data, cost tracking, and build readiness accurate day to day.

Alongside that, expect ongoing supplier relationship management, negotiating capacity and tooling maintenance windows, and cross-functional coordination with engineering, manufacturing, and quality on schedules and risk mitigation.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES;


1. Leadership & Team Development

 - Build, lead, and mentor a team of category specialists with deep mechanical hardware and manufacturing-support expertise.

 - Define team workflows spanning build-to-print CNC components, electromechanical release mechanisms, COTS mechanical hardware, production tooling, and consumables.

 - Coach team members in mechanical fabrication processes, tolerance/fit considerations, GD&T interpretation, and manufacturability constraints.

 - Foster a culture of technical rigor, proactive risk management, and high accountability.

 - Develop hiring profiles and long-term talent strategies to scale the category organization.
   

2. Embedded Technical Category Leadership

 - Operate as a core, embedded member of engineering and production project teams from concept through qualification and series production.

 - Interpret mechanical drawings, GD&T tolerances, material specifications, and BOM structures for build-to-print and COTS mechanical items.

 - Provide DFM/DFMA and supply feasibility input on mechanical designs, including release mechanisms and other electromechanical assemblies.

 - Identify long-lead mechanical items, critical single-source mechanisms, and production-tooling dependencies early in the design and industrialization cycle.

 - Maintain visibility into machining capabilities, surface treatments, mechanism qualification status, and tooling/jig availability across the supplier base.
   

3. High-Velocity Sourcing & Procurement Execution

 - Lead sourcing for:
   
   - Build-to-print CNC mechanical components
   
   - Electromechanical release mechanisms
   
   - COTS mechanical hardware (fasteners, bearings, standard hardware)
   
   - Production consumables and protective/PPE equipment
   
   - Production tooling, jigs, and fixtures
   
   - Tooling maintenance services
   
   - Third-party consulting and technical services

 - Approve or direct procurement at risk when required to protect program schedules.

 - Guide the team in fast-turn quoting, vendor selection, and build execution for precision-machined and electromechanical parts.

 - Ensure accurate procurement execution through ERP, with proper traceability, cost tracking, and build/production readiness visibility.
   

4. Supplier Engagement & Capability Development

 - Own senior relationships with precision machine shops, mechanism suppliers, tooling partners, PPE/consumables distributors, and technical services providers.

 - Perform technical capability assessments to ensure supplier fit for qualified, low-volume, and scaling production builds, including regulated/defense-sector requirements where applicable.

 - Negotiate accelerated build slots, exotic material availability, advanced machining tolerances, and priority manufacturing/tooling maintenance windows.

 - Develop a robust, internationally diversified supplier ecosystem capable of supporting both prototype builds and qualified series production.
   

5. Cross-Functional Collaboration & Strategic Alignment

 - Act as the senior supply chain voice for mechanical systems and manufacturing enablement across engineering, program management, manufacturing, quality, and executive forums.

 - Ensure alignment on engineering changes, mechanical drawing revisions, tooling readiness, and supply risks.

 - Translate evolving technical and regulatory requirements into executable category strategies.

 - Communicate proactively on risk, mitigation plans, and dependencies critical to program success.

 - Collaborate with Global Supply Chain leadership to build scalable capabilities supporting the transition from R&D to production.
   

6. Risk Management & Development-to-Production Continuity

 - Identify risks related to mechanical component availability, machining complexity, tooling capacity, mechanism qualification, and export/regulatory constraints.

 - Surface risks early in the design cycle and ensure visibility at key program milestones (PDR, CDR, PRR).

 - Drive early evaluation of alternates for materials, mechanisms, fabrication methods, and tooling solutions.

 - Support the transition toward Continuous Production Configurations by scaling sourcing strategies for mechanical hardware and production enablement.
   


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, Manufacturing Engineering, or similar technical discipline.

 - 7+ years in mechanical sourcing, manufacturing engineering, or category management roles, with a proven track record of team leadership in a management position (ideally leading 5+ team members).

 - Deep technical knowledge of:
   
   - Build-to-print CNC machining and mechanical tolerancing
   
   - Electromechanical release mechanisms and their qualification requirements
   
   - COTS mechanical hardware
   
   - Production tooling, jigs, fixtures, and tooling maintenance
   
   - Production consumables and PPE requirements

 - International experience, with demonstrated ability to manage a globally distributed supplier base.

 - Experience operating in highly regulated environments (e.g., aerospace, defense, or similarly certified industries).

 - Strong communication, negotiation, coaching, and cross-functional leadership skills.

 - Ability to translate mechanical engineering and manufacturing requirements into actionable category strategy.

 - Basic understanding of inventory control, stock accuracy, and material traceability

 - Experience using ERP, WMS, or similar systems for warehouse and inventory operations

description:
Role Highlights:

 - Department: Global Manufacturing Organization

 - Reports to: Stock & Logistics Manager

 - Location: Valencia, Spain

 - Type of Contract: Permanent

 - Working model: On-site

About the role

ICEYE is looking for a Warehouse / Logistics Operator to support the day-to-day flow of materials, components, and equipment within our manufacturing operations in Spain.

You will work closely with the Stock & Logistics Manager and manufacturing teams to ensure materials are received, checked, stored, picked, moved, and delivered to the right place at the right time. Your work will directly support production and AIT activities and help ensure that our teams have the materials they need to build and test satellites.

This is a hands-on role in a growing manufacturing environment where processes and systems are continuously being developed. You will be expected to work with accuracy and discipline, follow established procedures, keep the warehouse organised, and raise issues when something is not correct.

The role will cover warehouse operations, inventory handling, inbound and outbound shipments, material preparation, packaging, and system transactions. You will also support the safe handling and traceability of sensitive and high-value components.



Who We Are
ICEYE is the world leader in sovereign intelligence from space. We deliver persistent monitoring capabilities to detect and respond to changes in any location on Earth.

ICEYE owns the world's largest and most advanced SAR (synthetic aperture radar) satellite constellation. To our customers we provide intelligence with unmatched quality, latency and revisit times, in any weather, day or night. To governments who choose to operate their own constellation we provide this proven capability as a sovereign system.

ICEYE-built constellations serve customers in defence and intelligence, environmental monitoring, insurance and emergency management. We enable fast decisions that contribute to a safer future.

Founded and headquartered in Finland, ICEYE operates globally with over 1000 employees across Europe, North America, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.



What you will do

 - Receive incoming materials, components, and deliveries, checking quantities, identification, and documentation, and recording transactions in ERP or WMS systems

 - Store, label, and segregate materials to ensure proper identification and traceability, maintaining a clean and organised warehouse

 - Pick, prepare, and deliver materials and components to production and AIT areas according to requirements

 - Prepare, pack, and support inbound and outbound shipments, ensuring items are properly protected, labelled, and documented, coordinating with carriers when required

 - Perform inventory counts and cycle counting to support stock accuracy and reconciliation, escalating discrepancies to the Stock Manager

 - Handle sensitive, high-value, and fragile components safely, following material traceability, quarantine, and non-conforming material procedures

 - Support the resolution of material and logistics issues by working closely with the Stock Manager, Production, AIT, and Quality teams

 - Identify and escalate material discrepancies, inventory issues, or warehouse operational problems

 - Support the safe handling and movement of materials and equipment in line with applicable safety requirements

 - Maintain a clean, organised, and safe warehouse and logistics area at all times

 - Contribute to workplace organisation and continuous improvement activities, including 5S, standard work, and visual management

 - Support the Stock Manager in implementing and improving warehouse processes as the Spain manufacturing operation grows
   



What we’re looking for

Must haves:

 - Previous experience in warehouse, logistics, material handling, or a similar operational environment

 - Experience receiving, storing, picking, and issuing materials in a structured manufacturing or warehouse setting

 - Basic understanding of inventory control, stock accuracy, and material traceability

 - Experience using ERP, WMS, or similar systems for warehouse and inventory operations

 - Strong attention to detail and a disciplined approach to following processes

 - Comfortable working hands-on in a warehouse and manufacturing environment, including safe handling and movement of materials

 - Good communication skills in English, with the ability to work across production, engineering, quality, and logistics teams



Nice to haves:

 - Experience in aerospace, space, defence, automotive, or another high-reliability manufacturing environment

 - Experience with high-value, sensitive, serialised, or controlled components

 - Experience with international inbound/outbound shipments, customs documentation, or freight forwarding

 - Forklift certification or experience operating relevant warehouse equipment

 - Experience participating in Lean or continuous improvement activities
